chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from Muhammad ibn Uramah, from Abu Abdillah al-Mu'min, from Ibn Muskān, from Sulaym ibn Khālid, who said:

I heard Abā 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) say: It is strange for some people who claim to be our Shī'ah, and it is said that one of them passes his lifetime without visiting the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), due to negligence from it, and [contempt, and weakness, and laziness; he was contemptuous, weak, and lazy]. By Allah, if they knew what is in it of merit, they would not be contemptuous or lazy. I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, and what is in it of merit?' He said, 'There is much merit and goodness. Indeed, the first thing that befalls him is that his past sins are forgiven, and he is told to resume his deeds.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be him) critiques the paradox of those who claim allegiance to the Ahl al-Bayt yet neglect the grave of Imām al-Ḥusayn (peace be him) due to spiritual inertia or contempt. He highlights that the immediate reward for this Ziyārah is the forgiveness of past sins, serving as a powerful motivator to overcome laziness. This narration underscores the centrality of the Imams' graves in Shia identity through active devotion to the martyrdom of the third Imam, a key theme in Shia piety.
